verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν διδάσκοντος αὐτοῦ τὸν λαὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ εὐαγγελιζομένου ἐπέστησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς σὺν τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις
verses.transliteration: Kai egeneto en mia tōn hēmerōn didaskontos autou ton laon en tō hierō kai euangelizomenou epestēsan hoi archiereis kai hoi grammateis syn tois presbyterois
verses.literal: - One day as Jesus was teaching the people in the temple courts and proclaiming the gospel the chief priests and scribes together with the elders came up to Him
verses.literalPt: E ACONTECEU num daqueles dias que, estando ele ensinando o povo no templo, e anunciando o evangelho, sobrevieram os principais dos sacerdotes e os escribas com os anciãos,

verses.original: καὶ εἶπαν λέγοντες πρὸς αὐτόν Εἰπὸν ἡμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς ἢ τίς ἐστιν ὁ δούς σοι τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην
verses.transliteration: kai eipan legontes pros auton Eipon hēmin en poia exousia tauta poieis ē tis estin ho dous soi tēn exousian tautēn
verses.literal: Tell us - they said - by what authority are You doing these things and who - gave You this authority
verses.literalPt: E falaram-lhe, dizendo: Dize-nos, com que autoridade fazes estas coisas? Ou, quem é que te deu esta autoridade?

verses.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ἐρωτήσω ὑμᾶς κἀγὼ λόγον καὶ εἴπατέ μοι
verses.transliteration: Apokritheis de eipen pros autous Erōtēsō hymas kagō logon kai eipate moi
verses.literal: I will also ask you a question - Jesus replied - Tell Me
verses.literalPt: E, respondendo ele, disse-lhes: Também eu vos farei uma pergunta: Dizei-me pois:

verses.original: Τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἦν ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων
verses.transliteration: To baptisma Iōannou ex ouranou ēn ē ex anthrōpōn
verses.literal: John’s baptism was it from heaven or from men
verses.literalPt: O batismo de João era do céu ou dos homens?

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ συνελογίσαντο πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντες ὅτι Ἐὰν εἴπωμεν Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐρεῖ Διὰ τί οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Hoi de synelogisanto pros heautous legontes hoti Ean eipōmen Ex ouranou erei Dia ti ouk episteusate autō
verses.literal: They deliberated among themselves and said If we say From heaven He will ask Why . . . did you not believe him
verses.literalPt: E eles arrazoavam entre si, dizendo: Se dissermos: Do céu, ele nos dirá: Então por que o não crestes?

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπωμεν Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ὁ λαὸς ἅπας καταλιθάσει ἡμᾶς πεπεισμένος γάρ ἐστιν Ἰωάννην προφήτην εἶναι
verses.transliteration: ean de eipōmen Ex anthrōpōn ho laos hapas katalithasei hēmas pepeismenos gar estin Iōannēn prophētēn einai
verses.literal: But if we say From men all the people will stone us for they are convinced that John was a prophet
verses.literalPt: E se dissermos: Dos homens; todo o povo nos apedrejará, pois têm por certo que João era profeta.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀπεκρίθησαν μὴ εἰδέναι πόθεν
verses.transliteration: Kai apekrithēsan mē eidenai pothen
verses.literal: So they answered that they did not know where it was from
verses.literalPt: E responderam que não sabiam de onde era.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ
verses.transliteration: Kai ho Iēsous eipen autois Oude egō legō hymin en poia exousia tauta poiō
verses.literal: And Jesus replied . . . Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things
verses.literalPt: E Jesus lhes disse: Tampouco vos direi com que autoridade faço isto.

verses.original: Ἤρξατο δὲ πρὸς τὸν λαὸν λέγειν τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην Ἄνθρωπος τις ἐφύτευσεν ἀμπελῶνα καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν χρόνους ἱκανούς
verses.transliteration: Ērxato de pros ton laon legein tēn parabolēn tautēn Anthrōpos tis ephyteusen ampelōna kai exedeto auton geōrgois kai apedēmēsen chronous hikanous
verses.literal: Then He proceeded to tell the people this parable A man planted a vineyard rented it out to some tenants and went away for a long time
verses.literalPt: E começou a dizer ao povo esta parábola: Certo homem plantou uma vinha, e arrendou-a a uns lavradores, e partiu para fora da terra por muito tempo;

verses.original: καὶ καιρῷ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς δοῦλον ἵνα ἀπὸ τοῦ καρποῦ τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος δώσουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ δὲ γεωργοὶ ἐξαπέστειλαν αὐτὸν δείραντες κενόν
verses.transliteration: kai kairō apesteilen pros tous geōrgous doulon hina apo tou karpou tou ampelōnos dōsousin autō hoi de geōrgoi exapesteilan auton deirantes kenon
verses.literal: At harvest time he sent a servant to the tenants to collect . . . his share of the fruit of the vineyard But the tenants beat the servant and sent him away . . . empty-handed
verses.literalPt: E no tempo próprio mandou um servo aos lavradores, para que lhe dessem dos frutos da vinha; mas os lavradores, espancando-o, mandaram-no vazio.

verses.original: Καὶ προσέθετο ἕτερον πέμψαι δοῦλον οἱ δὲ κἀκεῖνον δείραντες καὶ ἀτιμάσαντες ἐξαπέστειλαν κενόν
verses.transliteration: Kai prosetheto heteron pempsai doulon hoi de kakeinon deirantes kai atimasantes exapesteilan kenon
verses.literal: So he sent another servant but they beat him and treated him shamefully . . . sending him away empty-handed
verses.literalPt: E tornou ainda a mandar outro servo; mas eles, espancando também a este, e afrontando-o, mandaram-no vazio.

verses.original: Καὶ προσέθετο τρίτον πέμψαι οἱ δὲ καὶ τοῦτον τραυματίσαντες ἐξέβαλον
verses.transliteration: Kai prosetheto triton pempsai hoi de kai touton traumatisantes exebalon
verses.literal: Then he sent a third but . . . they wounded him and threw him out
verses.literalPt: E tornou ainda a mandar um terceiro; mas eles, ferindo também a este, o expulsaram.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος Τί ποιήσω πέμψω τὸν υἱόν μου τὸν ἀγαπητόν ἴσως τοῦτον ἐντραπήσονται
verses.transliteration: Eipen de ho kyrios tou ampelōnos Ti poiēsō pempsō ton huion mou ton agapēton isōs touton entrapēsontai
verses.literal: What shall I do asked the owner of the vineyard I will send my beloved son Perhaps they will respect him
verses.literalPt: E disse o senhor da vinha: Que farei? Mandarei o meu filho amado; talvez, vendo-o, seja respeitado.

verses.original: Ἰδόντες δὲ αὐτὸν οἱ γεωργοὶ διελογίζοντο πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτόν ἵνα ἡμῶν γένηται ἡ κληρονομία
verses.transliteration: Idontes de auton hoi geōrgoi dielogizonto pros allēlous legontes Houtos estin ho klēronomos apokteinōmen auton hina hēmōn genētai hē klēronomia
verses.literal: But when the tenants saw the son they discussed it among themselves and said This is the heir Let us kill him and the inheritance will be ours
verses.literalPt: Mas, vendo-o os lavradores, arrazoaram entre si, dizendo: Este é o herdeiro; vinde, matemo-lo, para que a herança seja nossa.

verses.original: καὶ ἐκβαλόντες αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος ἀπέκτειναν Τί οὖν ποιήσει αὐτοῖς ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος
verses.transliteration: kai ekbalontes auton exō tou ampelōnos apekteinan Ti oun poiēsei autois ho kyrios tou ampelōnos
verses.literal: So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him What then will the owner of the vineyard do to them
verses.literalPt: E, lançando-o fora da vinha, o mataram. Que lhes fará, pois, o SENHOR da vinha?

verses.original: ἐλεύσεται καὶ ἀπολέσει τοὺς γεωργοὺς τούτους καὶ δώσει τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἄλλοις Ἀκούσαντες δὲ εἶπαν Μὴ γένοιτο
verses.transliteration: eleusetai kai apolesei tous geōrgous toutous kai dōsei ton ampelōna allois Akousantes de eipan Mē genoito
verses.literal: He will come and kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others And when the people heard this they said May such a thing never happen
verses.literalPt: Irá, e destruirá estes lavradores, e dará a outros a vinha. E, ouvindo eles isto, disseram: Não seja assim!

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ ἐμβλέψας αὐτοῖς εἶπεν Τί οὖν ἐστιν τὸ γεγραμμένον τοῦτο Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες Οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας
verses.transliteration: Ho de emblepsas autois eipen Ti oun estin to gegrammenon touto Lithon hon apedokimasan hoi oikodomountes Houtos egenēthē eis kephalēn gōnias
verses.literal: But Jesus looked directly at them and said Then what is the meaning of that which is written The stone the builders rejected has become . . . the cornerstone . . .
verses.literalPt: Mas ele, olhando para eles, disse: Que é isto, pois, que está escrito? A pedra, que os edificadores reprovaram, Essa foi feita cabeça da esquina.

verses.original: Πᾶς ὁ πεσὼν ἐπ’ ἐκεῖνον τὸν λίθον συνθλασθήσεται ἐφ’ ὃν δ’ ἂν πέσῃ λικμήσει αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Pas ho pesōn ep’ ekeinon ton lithon synthlasthēsetai eph’ hon d’ an pesē likmēsei auton
verses.literal: Everyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces but he on whom . . . it falls will be crushed . . .
verses.literalPt: Qualquer que cair sobre aquela pedra ficará em pedaços, e aquele sobre quem ela cair será feito em pó.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐζήτησαν οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐπιβαλεῖν ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸν λαόν ἔγνωσαν γὰρ ὅτι πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην
verses.transliteration: Kai ezētēsan hoi grammateis kai hoi archiereis epibalein ep’ auton tas cheiras en autē tē hōra kai ephobēthēsan ton laon egnōsan gar hoti pros autous eipen tēn parabolēn tautēn
verses.literal: When the scribes and chief priests realized that Jesus had spoken this parable against them they sought to arrest . . . . . . . . . Him that very hour But they were afraid of the people
verses.literalPt: E os principais dos sacerdotes e os escribas procuravam lançar mão dele naquela mesma hora; mas temeram o povo; porque entenderam que contra eles dissera esta parábola.

verses.original: Καὶ παρατηρήσαντες ἀπέστειλαν ἐνκαθέτους ὑποκρινομένους ἑαυτοὺς δικαίους εἶναι ἵνα ἐπιλάβωνται αὐτοῦ λόγου ὥστε παραδοῦναι αὐτὸν τῇ ἀρχῇ καὶ τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος
verses.transliteration: Kai paratērēsantes apesteilan enkathetous hypokrinomenous heautous dikaious einai hina epilabōntai autou logou hōste paradounai auton tē archē kai tē exousia tou hēgemonos
verses.literal: So they watched Him closely and sent spies who pretended to be sincere They were hoping to catch Him in His words in order to hand Him over . . . to the rule and authority of the governor
verses.literalPt: E, observando-o, mandaram espias, que se fingissem justos, para o apanharem nalguma palavra, e o entregarem à jurisdição e poder do presidente.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες Διδάσκαλε οἴδαμεν ὅτι ὀρθῶς λέγεις καὶ διδάσκεις καὶ οὐ λαμβάνεις πρόσωπον ἀλλ’ ἐπ’ ἀληθείας τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ διδάσκεις
verses.transliteration: kai epērōtēsan auton legontes Didaskale oidamen hoti orthōs legeis kai didaskeis kai ou lambaneis prosōpon all’ ep’ alētheias tēn hodon tou Theou didaskeis
verses.literal: Teacher they inquired . . . . . . we know that You speak and teach correctly You show no partiality . . . . . . but teach the way of God in accordance with the truth
verses.literalPt: E perguntaram-lhe, dizendo: Mestre, nós sabemos que falas e ensinas bem e retamente, e que não consideras a aparência da pessoa, mas ensinas com verdade o caminho de Deus.

verses.original: ἔξεστιν ἡμᾶς Καίσαρι φόρον δοῦναι ἢ οὔ
verses.transliteration: exestin hēmas Kaisari phoron dounai ē ou
verses.literal: Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not
verses.literalPt: É-nos lícito dar tributo a César ou não?

verses.original: Κατανοήσας δὲ αὐτῶν τὴν πανουργίαν εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: Katanoēsas de autōn tēn panourgian eipen pros autous
verses.literal: But Jesus saw through their duplicity and said to them
verses.literalPt: E, entendendo ele a sua astúcia, disse-lhes: Por que me tentais?

verses.original: Δείξατέ μοι δηνάριον τίνος ἔχει εἰκόνα καὶ ἐπιγραφήν Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Καίσαρος
verses.transliteration: Deixate moi dēnarion tinos echei eikona kai epigraphēn Hoi de eipan Kaisaros
verses.literal: Show Me a denarius Whose image and inscription are on it Caesar’s - they answered
verses.literalPt: Mostrai-me uma moeda. De quem tem a imagem e a inscrição? E, respondendo eles, disseram: De César.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Τοίνυν ἀπόδοτε τὰ Καίσαρος Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ τῷ Θεῷ
verses.transliteration: Ho de eipen pros autous Toinyn apodote ta Kaisaros Kaisari kai ta tou Theou tō Theō
verses.literal: So Jesus told . . . them Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s and to God what is God’s
verses.literalPt: Disse-lhes então: Dai, pois, a César o que é de César, e a Deus o que é de Deus.

verses.original: Καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν ἐπιλαβέσθαι αὐτοῦ ῥήματος ἐναντίον τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ θαυμάσαντες ἐπὶ τῇ ἀποκρίσει αὐτοῦ ἐσίγησαν
verses.transliteration: Kai ouk ischysan epilabesthai autou rhēmatos enantion tou laou kai thaumasantes epi tē apokrisei autou esigēsan
verses.literal: And they were unable to trap Him in His words before the people And amazed at His answer they fell silent
verses.literalPt: E não puderam apanhá-lo em palavra alguma diante do povo; e, maravilhados da sua resposta, calaram-se.

verses.original: Προσελθόντες δέ τινες τῶν Σαδδουκαίων οἱ ἀντιλέγοντες ἀνάστασιν μὴ εἶναι ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν
verses.transliteration: Proselthontes de tines tōn Saddoukaiōn hoi antilegontes anastasin mē einai epērōtēsan auton
verses.literal: Then some of the Sadducees who say there is no . . . . . . resurrection came to question Him
verses.literalPt: E, chegando-se alguns dos saduceus, que dizem não haver ressurreição, perguntaram-lhe,

verses.original: λέγοντες Διδάσκαλε Μωϋσῆς ἔγραψεν ἡμῖν ἐάν τινος ἀδελφὸς ἀποθάνῃ ἔχων γυναῖκα καὶ οὗτος ἄτεκνος ᾖ ἵνα λάβῃ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ ἐξαναστήσῃ σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: legontes Didaskale Mōusēs egrapsen hēmin ean tinos adelphos apothanē echōn gynaika kai houtos ateknos ē hina labē ho adelphos autou tēn gynaika kai exanastēsē sperma tō adelphō autou
verses.literal: Teacher they said Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him
verses.literalPt: Dizendo: Mestre, Moisés nos deixou escrito que, se o irmão de algum falecer, tendo mulher, e não deixar filhos, o irmão dele tome a mulher, e suscite posteridade a seu irmão.

verses.original: ἑπτὰ οὖν ἀδελφοὶ ἦσαν καὶ ὁ πρῶτος λαβὼν γυναῖκα ἀπέθανεν ἄτεκνος
verses.transliteration: hepta oun adelphoi ēsan kai ho prōtos labōn gynaika apethanen ateknos
verses.literal: Now there were seven brothers The first one married a wife but died childless
verses.literalPt: Houve, pois, sete irmãos, e o primeiro tomou mulher, e morreu sem filhos;

verses.original: καὶ ὁ δεύτερος
verses.transliteration: kai ho deuteros
verses.literal: Then the second
verses.literalPt: E tomou-a o segundo por mulher, e ele morreu sem filhos.

verses.original: καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἔλαβεν αὐτήν ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ οἱ ἑπτὰ οὐ κατέλιπον τέκνα καὶ ἀπέθανον
verses.transliteration: kai ho tritos elaben autēn hōsautōs de kai hoi hepta ou katelipon tekna kai apethanon
verses.literal: and the third married the widow and in the same way . . . all seven died leaving no children
verses.literalPt: E tomou-a o terceiro, e igualmente também os sete; e morreram, e não deixaram filhos.

verses.original: ὕστερον καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἀπέθανεν
verses.transliteration: hysteron kai hē gynē apethanen
verses.literal: And last of all the woman died
verses.literalPt: E por último, depois de todos, morreu também a mulher.

verses.original: ἡ γυνὴ οὖν ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τίνος αὐτῶν γίνεται γυνή οἱ γὰρ ἑπτὰ ἔσχον αὐτὴν γυναῖκα
verses.transliteration: hē gynē oun en tē anastasei tinos autōn ginetai gynē hoi gar hepta eschon autēn gynaika
verses.literal: So then in the resurrection - whose . . . wife will she be For all seven were married to her
verses.literalPt: Portanto, na ressurreição, de qual deles será a mulher, pois que os sete por mulher a tiveram?

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου γαμοῦσιν καὶ γαμίσκονται
verses.transliteration: Kai eipen autois ho Iēsous Hoi huioi tou aiōnos toutou gamousin kai gamiskontai
verses.literal: Jesus answered . . . The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage
verses.literalPt: E, respondendo Jesus, disse-lhes: Os filhos deste mundo casam-se, e dão-se em casamento;

verses.original: οἱ δὲ καταξιωθέντες τοῦ αἰῶνος ἐκείνου τυχεῖν καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τῆς ἐκ νεκρῶν οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται
verses.transliteration: hoi de kataxiōthentes tou aiōnos ekeinou tychein kai tēs anastaseōs tēs ek nekrōn oute gamousin oute gamizontai
verses.literal: But those who are considered worthy to share in the age to come and in the resurrection from the dead will neither marry nor be given in marriage
verses.literalPt: Mas os que forem havidos por dignos de alcançar o mundo vindouro, e a ressurreição dentre os mortos, nem hão de casar, nem ser dados em casamento;

verses.original: οὐδὲ γὰρ ἀποθανεῖν ἔτι δύνανται ἰσάγγελοι γάρ εἰσιν καὶ υἱοί εἰσιν Θεοῦ τῆς ἀναστάσεως υἱοὶ ὄντες
verses.transliteration: oude gar apothanein eti dynantai isangeloi gar eisin kai huioi eisin Theou tēs anastaseōs huioi ontes
verses.literal: In fact they can no longer die because they are like the angels And since they are sons of the resurrection they are sons of God
verses.literalPt: Porque já não podem mais morrer; pois são iguais aos anjos, e são filhos de Deus, sendo filhos da ressurreição.

verses.original: Ὅτι δὲ ἐγείρονται οἱ νεκροὶ καὶ Μωϋσῆς ἐμήνυσεν ἐπὶ τῆς Βάτου ὡς λέγει Κύριον Τὸν Θεὸν Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Θεὸν Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Θεὸν Ἰακώβ
verses.transliteration: Hoti de egeirontai hoi nekroi kai Mōusēs emēnysen epi tēs Batou hōs legei Kyrion Ton Theon Abraam kai Theon Isaak kai Theon Iakōb
verses.literal: Even Moses demonstrates that the dead are raised in the passage about the burning bush For he calls the Lord the God of Abraham the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob
verses.literalPt: E que os mortos hão de ressuscitar também o mostrou Moisés junto da sarça, quando chama ao Senhor Deus de Abraão, e Deus de Isaque, e Deus de Jacó.

verses.original: Θεὸς δὲ οὐκ ἔστιν νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων πάντες γὰρ αὐτῷ ζῶσιν
verses.transliteration: Theos de ouk estin nekrōn alla zōntōn pantes gar autō zōsin
verses.literal: He is not the God of the dead but of the living for to Him all are alive
verses.literalPt: Ora, Deus não é Deus de mortos, mas de vivos; porque para ele vivem todos.

verses.original: Ἀποκριθέντες δέ τινες τῶν γραμματέων εἶπαν Διδάσκαλε καλῶς εἶπας
verses.transliteration: Apokrithentes de tines tōn grammateōn eipan Didaskale kalōs eipas
verses.literal: Some of the scribes answered . . . Teacher You have spoken well
verses.literalPt: E, respondendo alguns dos escribas, disseram: Mestre, disseste bem.

verses.original: οὐκέτι γὰρ ἐτόλμων ἐπερωτᾶν αὐτὸν οὐδέν
verses.transliteration: ouketi gar etolmōn eperōtan auton ouden
verses.literal: And they did not dare to question Him any further
verses.literalPt: E não ousavam perguntar-lhe mais coisa alguma.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς Πῶς λέγουσιν τὸν Χριστὸν εἶναι Δαυὶδ υἱόν
verses.transliteration: Eipen de pros autous Pōs legousin ton Christon einai Dauid huion
verses.literal: Then Jesus declared . . . . . . How can it be said that the Christ is the Son of David
verses.literalPt: E ele lhes disse: Como dizem que o Cristo é filho de Davi?

verses.original: αὐτὸς γὰρ Δαυὶδ λέγει ἐν βίβλῳ ψαλμῶν Εἶπεν Κύριος τῷ Κυρίῳ μου Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου
verses.transliteration: autos gar Dauid legei en biblō psalmōn Eipen Kyrios tō Kyriō mou Kathou ek dexiōn mou
verses.literal: For David himself says in the book of Psalms The Lord said to my Lord Sit at My right hand
verses.literalPt: Visto como o mesmo Davi diz no livro dos Salmos: Disse o SENHOR ao meu Senhor: Assenta-te à minha direita,

verses.original: Ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου Ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου
verses.transliteration: Heōs an thō tous echthrous sou Hypopodion tōn podōn sou
verses.literal: until . . . I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet
verses.literalPt: Até que eu ponha os teus inimigos por escabelo de teus pés.

verses.original: Δαυὶδ οὖν αὐτὸν Κύριον καλεῖ καὶ πῶς αὐτοῦ υἱός ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: Dauid oun auton Kyrion kalei kai pōs autou huios estin
verses.literal: Thus David calls Him Lord So how can He be David’s son
verses.literalPt: Se Davi lhe chama Senhor, como é ele seu filho?

verses.original: Ἀκούοντος δὲ παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Akouontos de pantos tou laou eipen tois mathētais autou
verses.literal: In the hearing of all the people Jesus said to His disciples
verses.literalPt: E, ouvindo-o todo o povo, disse Jesus aos seus discípulos:

verses.original: Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν γραμματέων τῶν θελόντων περιπατεῖν ἐν στολαῖς καὶ φιλούντων ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ πρωτοκλισίας ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις
verses.transliteration: Prosechete apo tōn grammateōn tōn thelontōn peripatein en stolais kai philountōn aspasmous en tais agorais kai prōtokathedrias en tais synagōgais kai prōtoklisias en tois deipnois
verses.literal: Beware of the scribes They like to walk around in long robes and they love the greetings in the marketplaces the chief seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets
verses.literalPt: Guardai-vos dos escribas, que querem andar com vestes compridas; e amam as saudações nas praças, e as principais cadeiras nas sinagogas, e os primeiros lugares nos banquetes;

verses.original: οἳ κατεσθίουσιν τὰς οἰκίας τῶν χηρῶν καὶ προφάσει μακρὰ προσεύχονται οὗτοι λήμψονται περισσότερον κρίμα
verses.transliteration: hoi katesthiousin tas oikias tōn chērōn kai prophasei makra proseuchontai houtoi lēmpsontai perissoteron krima
verses.literal: They defraud widows of their houses and for a show make lengthy prayers These men will receive greater condemnation
verses.literalPt: Que devoram as casas das viúvas, fazendo, por pretexto, longas orações. Estes receberão maior condenação.
